passages.text: Stream bonding initially blackholed: Xray 26.x freedom outbound looping back into the merge daemon (127.0.0.1:7443) swallowed traffic. Fixed in v0.6.2 (S11) via the finalRules patch (server/setup-xray-reality.sh, idempotent) + PING/PONG carrier verification before a carrier is schedulable.

nodes.title: Reorder-buffer overflow during saturation shifts — hard session error instead of backpressure (addressed in S14 WIP)

passages.text: During saturation shifts the reorder buffer could overflow its 4 MiB cap and fail the whole session. S14 WIP: cap raised to 16 MiB and a backpressure path added (ReorderBuffer::would_overflow; the endpoint holds the frame up to REORDER_PAUSE_MAX 5 s — carrier TCP backpressure throttles the sender while the gap drains; soft cap afterwards).

nodes.title: Uneven traffic split under saturation — one adapter maxes out, excess does NOT spill to remaining adapters

passages.text: User-reported (recurring): traffic is not being split evenly; when one adapter reaches its maximum bandwidth range, the rest of the traffic does not split over to the remaining adapters. First addressed by D23/v0.7.0 (balanced pressure + priority ramp-spill) for the per-connection path; the stream-bonding frame scheduler had no saturation signal, so a maxed-out carrier kept receiving frames. S14 fix implemented + gated (peer-reported delivery rates; see task:saturation-aware-split) — awaiting release v0.8.0 and real-setup verification before closing.

nodes.title: D29 P0 reconnect force-close + bind retry

passages.text: Second-connection bug root cause: untracked connection tasks pinned listener-port sockets past the drain; Windows re-bind WSAEADDRINUSE (Linux tolerates re-bind over non-listening sockets — proven by scripts/rebind_probe.rs). Fix: Shared.conns AbortHandles + end-of-drain force-close + AbortPumpsOnDrop (pumps detach on JoinHandle drop) + bind_with_retry 5s. engine_file_stem FNV identity hash separates same-tag profiles (H2); store_mtx serializes profiles.json RMW (H3). source=src/real_service.rs#connect

nodes.title: D30 QoS fair share + merged Exit&speed panel

passages.text: QoS: per-destination groups, 1 s tick refills aggregate/groups only under contention (>=2 groups AND >=2 MiB/s aggregate floor), pump read gate blocks until budget, scheduler ALWAYS attached so the Settings qos_fair toggle flips live (no reconnect). Merged Exit & speed Status panel (view-only merge, D24-safe, both triggers side-by-side). P1 parity: TCP_NODELAY x4 legs, ACK coalescing 8 frames/20ms with CLOSE+PING flush, same-carrier PONG echo (RTT was cross-contaminated), send-path copies 5->3 (encode_session_borrowed, wire-identity test), writev batching (<=16 frames), quarantine last-resort fallback (no sole-link blackout), production prober uses user probe target. source=crates/mt-net/src/qos.rs

nodes.title: MultiTunnel — Rust rewrite of BondTunnel; zero-dependency all-in-one (v2rayN import + net-merge), Material You GUI

passages.text: MultiTunnel: Rust rewrite of BondTunnel; zero-dependency all-in-one (v2rayN import + net-merge), Material You GUI. Repo: github.com/maniesh-NR/MultiTunnel. Windows client → local SOCKS/HTTP → ProxyServer → BondOutbound → N carriers (one per bonded NIC, VLESS+REALITY via Xray sendThrough, engine self-provisioned D14) → VM Xray (public 8443) → freedom → mt-merge-server (127.0.0.1:7443) → real target. Reverse symmetric. Auth at the Xray edge.

Two bond modes: per-connection (default) and stream bonding (D17 framing, needs the VM merge daemon; carriers verified by PING/PONG before schedulable). Scheduling (D23, v0.7.0): five merge policies in mt-net — round-robin, failover, lowest-latency (EWMA), balanced (stock default), priority (user order; fills #1 until bandwidth plateaus then spills). Stream-mode frame scheduler is policy-aware too. Adapter priority == saved bonded_adapters ORDER; Adapters tab = ordering UI.

Hard rules: config schema camelCase + versioned migrations (D8); no secrets in repo (D9) — token lives in ../upload/, backup.sh reads it; fail-open routing (D5); GUI never dies invisibly (D15); vendored iced under vendor/ + [patch.crates-io] (D21); CI timestamps UTC; rustc 1.100.0 + zig 0.14.1 + cargo-zigbuild (D2), windows target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu.

nodes.title: Agentic memory graph + RAG retrieval (S14) — typed nodes/edges store, BM25 + graph expansion, all-agent accessible

passages.text: The agentic memory is a typed graph store: harness/memory/store/memory_graph.json (schema v1). Nodes (whitelisted types: project, architecture, playbook, contract, state, decision, ledger, release, commit, task, bug, component, protocol, report, consensus, fact) carry retrieval passages; edges carry typed relations with evidence. Sources: PROJECT_MEMORY.md durable sections, STATE.md, DECISIONS.md, LEDGER.md (grouped per stage tag), agent-reports/, consensus/, git tags + full log, curated/.

RAG retrieval (BM25 k1=1.5 b=0.75, title boost 1.5, plus graph-neighborhood expansion with 0.5^hop score decay): query from repo root with `python3 query_memory.py "<topic>"` (flags: -k N, --expand HOPS, --json, --prompt). --prompt emits a paste-ready context pack with induced subgraph links — the RAG input for any consuming agent (session start, subagent delegation, or future session).

Agent WRITE path: `python3 harness/memory/write_memory.py --node id=... type=... title=... passage=...` or `--edge src=... dst=... rel=... evidence=...` — appends/updates harness/memory/curated/{nodes,edges}.json (merged last at build, wins on id collision) and rebuilds the store. update_memory.py rebuilds the store on every run. Rebuilds are deterministic (byte-identical while HEAD and sources are unchanged; no wall-clock in the store). Tests: python3 harness/memory/test_graph.py.

nodes.title: pstack — persistent external memory, zero-noise compaction, deep-first investigation, playbook execution

passages.text: pstack working agreement: persistent external memory, zero-noise compaction, deep-first investigation, playbook execution. Session ritual: git fetch && git rebase origin/main, then python3 update_memory.py, then read the Active Playbook section of PROJECT_MEMORY.md. Durable sections of PROJECT_MEMORY.md are maintained BY HAND; the recent-activity section is maintained BY SCRIPT. Long-form history lives in harness/memory/ (LEDGER.md append-only, STATE.md rewritten per stage, DECISIONS.md immutable).

Backup protocol: every roadmap stage ends with ./harness/backup.sh <label> (local commit + tag, pushes to GitHub main + tags when the token is available). Big stages use parallel adversarial agents with consensus gates (D6); agent reports land in harness/memory/agent-reports/, consensus in harness/memory/consensus/.
Never write the exact git-activity section header string anywhere above the section itself — update_memory.py splits on its first occurrence.

nodes.title: Task E (core) — saturation-aware redistribution: when one adapter hits its bandwidth ceiling, spill traffic to the rest (S14, gated — release pending)

passages.text: Task E core: user reported traffic still not split evenly — when one adapter reaches its maximum bandwidth, the remaining traffic does NOT split over to the remaining adapters. v0.7.0's balanced/priority (D23) spread per-connection load but stream-mode saturation spill was missing. S14 fix (started at commit f4a26ca, completed + gated this session): each endpoint measures per-carrier inbound rate and reports it to the peer piggybacked on 1 s PINGs; scheduler keeps EWMA assignment rate per carrier; carrier_score = assign_bps / max(deliver_bps, PROBE_BPS 32 KiB/s); Balanced picks least relative load (capacity-proportional spreading — aggregate = SUM of paths); Priority spills at score >= 1.15 (PRIORITY_SPILL_RATIO); reorder cap 4->16 MiB with a backpressure overflow path (would_overflow + REORDER_PAUSE) instead of failing the session; falls back to S12 least-queued behavior when the peer sends no reports. Gates passed: fmt, workspace clippy -D warnings, 404/0 workspace tests. REMAINING: windows-gnu clippy, zigbuild, release v0.8.0, real-setup verification.
